candidates.claim_theme: AI wildfire detection is a mature, broadly-deployed solution across the West (17 states) implying Alaska is covered or next
claim_verbatim_options: we never would have guessed we'd be sitting here in 2026 doing deployments in Georgia, in the Dakotas, in New Jersey
In some years, such as 2022, Alaska accounted for nearly half of the total U.S. acreage burned by wildfires.
candidates.received_wisdom: AI camera detection (Pano AI / ALERTWest) is now a proven, scaling wildfire tool across 17 western states, beating 911 calls by ~45 min; the implicit frame is Alaska benefits too.

counter_evidence.fact: ALERTWest network lists OR, WA, CA, ID, CO, HI, MT, NV — Alaska absent.
AICC program manager Heidi Strader (Nov 2025): the AI lightning-prediction tool 'still has some fine-tuning ahead' — not operational.
Pano AI / ADN wire (May 2026) on Western AI fire detection does not name Alaska as a participant.

candidates.load_bearing: Active June 2026 fire season; BLM Alaska, Alaska Division of Forestry, and ANCs managing millions of acres are making fire-season preparedness investments. Perception that AI fire detection is mature/coming could misdirect procurement.
candidates.attribution_note: Strong theme but the cleanest single verbatim asserter span needs validator confirmation; the received wisdom is an aggregate frame across WBUR/ADN/KPBS.

candidates.claim_theme: AI-powered battle management C2 is coming to Golden Dome (anchored at Fort Greely) and will change deployment + enable affordability
claim_verbatim_options: Another significant initiative for Golden Dome is the instantiation of an integrated, advanced and a resilient battle management command and control powered by AI.
candidates.received_wisdom: AI battle management for Golden Dome is imminent and is the lever that makes the system affordable and operationally superior; Fort Greely (holds ~40 of 44 U.S. GBIs) is central.

asserters.name: Marcia Holmes
asserters.title_or_org: Deputy Director for Golden Dome, U.S. DoD

counter_evidence.fact: CBO May 2026 estimates Golden Dome could cost $1.2 trillion over 20 years; the AI C2 layer has no separate cost estimate or funded program of record.
Existing Fort Greely fire control is a 'dual-node, human-in-control interface' (Fort Greely + Colorado Springs) — AI integration aspirational, not fielded.
Space Force selected 12 companies for Golden Dome space-based interceptors (Apr 2026), but the non-space sensor-fusion C2 AI layer has no separately funded program of record.

candidates.load_bearing: Fort Greely holds ~40 of 44 existing U.S. Ground-Based Interceptors. Defense contractors, AK appropriators, and workforce developers size investments against the premise AI C2 is imminent and affordability-enabling.
candidates.attribution_note: Cleanest defense candidate; single named DoD official, primary-source Breaking Defense quote, primary-source CBO counter.

candidates.claim_theme: AI compresses critical-mineral assessment from years to 2.5 days, implying near-term readiness for Alaska's mineral base
claim_verbatim_options: Hackathons have demonstrated the AI tools' ability to reduce the critical mineral assessment workflow to two and half days, start to finish.
candidates.received_wisdom: DARPA/USGS AI (CriticalMAAS) can cut Alaska critical-mineral assessment from ~2 years to days.

counter_evidence.fact: USGS Alaska Science Center (Dec 2025) describes ongoing multi-year graphite/lithium/REE surveys with no AI acceleration; lithium assessment still 'beginning'.
The 2.5-day result was the data-compilation step on a single deposit type (tungsten skarn) in controlled hackathon conditions, not full field-validated assessment in remote Alaska terrain.

candidates.load_bearing: Alaska holds Graphite Creek (largest known U.S. graphite) + REE/cobalt/nickel/antimony potential; allocators and miners time investment and due diligence on expected assessment speed.
candidates.attribution_note: Fresh; primary-source on both sides. Asserter quote is from DARPA news, slightly older (Jan 2025) but recurs in 2026 trade press.

candidates.claim_theme: AI will 'revolutionize' Alaska PFD processing (a 'game changer')
claim_verbatim_options: promises to revolutionize how we process PFD applications — a true game changer for generations of Alaskans
candidates.received_wisdom: Partnering with an AI consultant to modernize the PFD application system will fundamentally transform how Alaska processes dividends for 600,000+ residents.

asserters.name: Fadil Limani
asserters.title_or_org: Deputy Commissioner, Alaska Department of Revenue

counter_evidence.fact: Saige partner Charles Hu (same cycle): 'none of the systems are running automatically, and an analyst will still need to ensure that all application information is correct.' AI handles correspondence drafting + document ingestion, not eligibility determination.
Route Fifty (Jan 2025) describes system as 'expected to go live early next year'; no reporting confirms operational rollout as of June 2026.

candidates.load_bearing: PFD is the most politically sensitive state process (touches every resident). The 'revolutionize' claim shapes contractor accountability, legislative oversight, and the AI-in-government narrative statewide.
candidates.attribution_note: Cleanest single-asserter attribution; official verbatim quote; primary-source counter from the vendor itself. NOTE the quote contains 'revolutionize'/'game changer' which are banned in OUR copy but fine inside a quoted claim.

candidates.claim_theme: AI will streamline Alaska resource permitting (Dunleavy AO 360)
claim_verbatim_options: Leverage technology, such as artificial intelligence ('AI'), to support digitization, automation, and public access to permitting information
candidates.received_wisdom: Gov. Dunleavy's AO 360 (Aug 2025) directs DNR/DEC/DFG to use AI to digitize and speed permitting.

asserters.name: Mike Dunleavy
asserters.title_or_org: Governor of Alaska, via Administrative Order No. 360

counter_evidence.fact: DEC AO 360 implementation focused on regulatory text reduction; the AI directive carries no technology procurement, timeline, or system spec. Language is 'Leverage technology, such as AI' — aspirational.
UAF ACEP (Feb 2024): Alaska permit data is not systematically digitized; the foundation for AI-assisted permitting does not yet exist at scale.

candidates.load_bearing: Resource developers and federal contractors calibrate permit timelines and lobbying around whether AI-assisted permitting actually shortens review windows.
candidates.attribution_note: Fresh; official order verbatim; primary-source counter from the implementing agency.

candidates.claim_theme: DOE national-lab AI will streamline permitting for Alaska energy + critical-mineral projects
claim_verbatim_options: offer capabilities to streamline permitting for large-scale energy and critical mineral projects in Alaska
candidates.received_wisdom: Sen. Murkowski's DOE AI Act will let DOE national-lab AI accelerate Alaska energy + mineral permitting.

counter_evidence.fact: DOE has no national lab in or focused on Alaska; the bill targets Oak Ridge/Argonne/Sandia etc. Alaska permitting is governed by the state and Army Corps, not DOE — the mechanism is unspecified.
The actual AI-for-Alaska-minerals pipeline runs through USGS/DARPA CriticalMAAS, not the DOE labs this bill funds.

candidates.load_bearing: Alaska critical-mineral developers (Graphite One, North Slope cobalt/nickel) make capital decisions partly on expected permitting timelines.
candidates.attribution_note: Claim is from July 2024 — older; recurs in 2026 critical-minerals discourse. Mechanism-gap correction is sharp.

candidates.claim_theme: Alaska has taken NO coordinated AI policy action
claim_verbatim_options: Alaska has done none of that. No comprehensive policy, no clear direction, no coordinated strategy.
candidates.received_wisdom: Unlike the 38 states that passed AI/data-center laws in 2025, Alaska has done nothing coordinated on AI.

counter_evidence.fact: Alaska DEED published a statewide K-12 AI Strategic Framework Oct 2025 (32nd state to issue K-12 AI guidance).
Alaska HB 47 (AI-generated CSAM felony) passed the House 39-0 on Feb 27, 2026 — concrete AI legislation.
UAA launched the NSF-funded Alaska AI Solutions Consortium (Sept 2025).

candidates.load_bearing: Frames Alaska as a policy vacuum, shaping how allocators/program offices view the state as an AI partner and shaping the legislative agenda (HCR 3 died May 2026).
candidates.attribution_note: Editorial-board asserter (institutional, not individual). Counter-evidence is partly about adjacent domains (K-12, CSAM) vs the editorial's data-center-policy focus — steelman must be careful not to strawman.
